sentences.text: Tongtianlong was a sheep-sized, feathered theropod that ate both plants and meat.

The fossil was discovered in the Nanxiong Formation and is now kept at the Dongyang Museum. Its specific name, limosus, means muddy because the specimen was preserved in mudstone. Lü Junchang, Chen Rongjun, Stephen L. Brusatte, and colleagues first described this animal.
In 2016, Tongtianlong was classified as a member of the Oviraptoridae family, closely related to Banji and Wulatelong.
This creature lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian epoch.
It is the sixth oviraptorid described from the Nanxiong Formation, following Banji, Ganzhousaurus, Jiangxisaurus, Nankangia, and Huanansaurus.
It is debated whether some Nanxiong Formation oviraptorids represent growth stages of others or are genuinely distinct animals, though juvenile anatomy suggests they are likely distinct species.

While the diversity of Nanxiong Formation oviraptorids is suggested to indicate an evolutionary radiation prior to the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event, it remains possible that these species come from different time periods due to insufficient stratigraphic study.
